Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Our legal team attached a redline of Redwood's standard DPA (attached) and flagged a few areas we need clarity on before we can proceed to execution:

- Subprocessor list: can you confirm the current roster of subprocessors that may process EU personal data, and indicate which ones store data outside the EEA?
- Cross-border mechanism: we need to confirm whether Redwood relies on SCCs, BCRs, or a combination, and whether there are any vendor-specific addenda we should see.
- Audit rights: Helix requires annual evidence of SOC 2 Type II and a pen test summary, and explicit language for on-site/remote audit rights in limited circumstances.

Attached: Helix_DPA_redline_v3.docx (our proposed edits). Please let us know what evidence you can provide and whether Redwood can sign via DocuSign.

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + questions on subprocessors and transfers

Ethan —

Thanks for sending the redlines and the clear list of asks. Quick answers and next steps below, and I attached our SOC 2 summary and abbreviated pen test executive summary for your review.

Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a public subprocessor register; current EU-impacting subprocessors include: CloudEdge Storage (data persistence), FastQueue (async job routing), and MetricsLane (observability). CloudEdge and MetricsLane operate EU regions; FastQueue routes through a US-based cluster for burst. We'll provide an export of the register for your legal team.

Cross-border transfers: For customers headquartered in the EU we primarily use Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with a controller-to-processor addendum. For certain private deployments we can discuss model where the customer acts as controller/processor depending on config.

Audit rights/evidence: We can provide: 1) SOC 2 Type II summary (attached), 2) a pen-test executive summary (attached), and 3) a process to request scoping for remote evidence collection. We typically include a clause that allows an annual audit or an independent third-party assessment with reasonable notice; however, we prefer evidence packs in the first instance versus unfettered on-site audits.

DocuSign: Yes — we can execute via DocuSign. I can push a signed copy once we have agreed the narrow audit language.

Proposed next step: 30-minute touchpoint to walk the redline and agree the audit wording. Are you available next Tue (10/28) at 09:00 CET / 00:00 PT?

Attaching: SOC2-TypeII-summary.pdf, pen-test-exec-summary.pdf

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-summary.pdf, pen-test-exec-summary.pdf]

From: Dana Moss <dpo@dataguardhealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@helixhealth.com>
Cc: contracts@helixhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-28T08:32:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + questions on subprocessors and transfers

Hi Priyom / Ethan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the attachments. I reviewed the SOC2 summary and pen test exec note; helpful. A couple of clarifications before we proceed to signature:

1) Audit rights scope: Helix's procurement policy requires explicit contractual language that allows an annual compliance validation. We prefer evidence collection first, but we need the language to permit (i) remote evidence requests up to once per year by Helix or (ii) a third-party audit if remote evidence is insufficient, with Redwood covering reasonable costs only if non-compliance is found.
2) Subprocessor notifications: We need a 30-day notice window for new EU-impacting subprocessors.
3) SCCs: We would like to see a completed SCC annex in the DPA at signature if possible; otherwise, confirm that SCCs will be adopted and appended automatically on onboarding.

If Redwood can accept the limited audit wording above and commit to SCCs appended at execution, we can proceed to DocuSign the redline. If you could send a DocuSign envelope pre-populated with Redwood's final edits, that would speed things.

Thanks —
Dana Moss
DPO (acting)
Dataguard Health (on behalf of Helix procurement)

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Dana Moss <dpo@dataguardhealth.com>, Ethan Shaw <ethan.shaw@helixhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + questions on subprocessors and transfers

Dana / Ethan —

Appreciate the clarity. I've incorporated your requested audit language into the redline (see notes) and added a short SCC annex placeholder that gets completed at signature. Key points we adapted:

- Audit right: "Customer may request evidence of compliance once per 12-month period; if remote evidence is insufficient and an on-site or third-party audit is reasonably required, the parties will agree a scoping statement and Redwood will only bear costs if a material breach attributable to Redwood or its subprocessors is identified." (we kept costs carve to material breach only).
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood accepts a 30-day notification window for EU-impacting subprocessors; emergency operational exceptions apply with notification as soon as practicable.
- SCCs: SCC annex to be appended at signature; DocuSign envelope will contain the completed annex for Helix to review before final execution.

Sending DocuSign envelope now for execution: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/ABC123-Helix-HLX4521 (placeholder link). Please review the updated redline and sign. I've copied Marissa from Sales to confirm billing/contract ops once signed.

Best,
Priyom Das
